source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Every pregnant woman in the community must be registered in MoH 514 and supported to attend at least 8 ANC contacts at a health facility. Contact 1 should occur within the first 12 weeks of pregnancy. CHPs must track attendance and follow up missed appointments.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Any confirmed pregnant woman living in the community unit.
danger_signs: Missed first contact past 16 weeks gestation
More than 6 weeks overdue for scheduled facility contact
mandated_chw_actions: Register pregnancy in MoH 514 household register
Counsel on 8-contact schedule: Contact 1 (<12w), Contact 2 (20w), Contact 3 (26w), Contact 4 (30w), Contact 5 (34w), Contact 6 (36w), Contact 7 (38w), Contact 8 (40w)
Emphasize facility delivery with skilled birth attendant
Screen for early danger signs and initiate birth preparedness plan
negative_boundaries: Do not encourage or support planned home delivery
Do not delay registration until the third trimester
Do not refer to unregistered traditional birth attendants (TBAs)

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-01] ANC Booking & 8-Contact Schedule
CRITERIA: All pregnant women in the community.
ACTIONS: Register in MoH 514. Counsel on 8-contact schedule starting <12 weeks (then 20w, 26w, 30w, 34w, 36w, 38w, 40w). Promote skilled facility delivery and individual birth planning.
PROHIBITED: Do not endorse planned home delivery or traditional birth attendants.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Elevated blood pressure (systolic >= 140 mmHg or diastolic >= 90 mmHg) after 20 weeks gestation is abnormal. If accompanied by severe headache, visual disturbances, epigastric pain, or proteinuria, it is pre-eclampsia and requires immediate hospital referral.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Gestation >= 20 weeks with SBP >= 140 mmHg OR DBP >= 90 mmHg.
danger_signs: Severe persistent frontal headache not relieved by rest or simple analgesics
Visual disturbances (blurred vision, double vision, flashing lights)
Severe pain in the upper abdomen (epigastric pain) or persistent vomiting
Swelling of hands, face, or sudden excessive weight gain
Convulsions or twitching (eclampsia)
mandated_chw_actions: Initiate IMMEDIATE emergency referral to Level 4 Hospital / CEmoNC facility
Position patient comfortably on her left side to optimize placental blood flow
Assist family in organizing emergency community transport and companion
Reassure family; keep patient calm and in a quiet environment
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not prescribe or administer oral or injectable antihypertensives at home (no nifedipine, labetalol, hydralazine)
STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not attempt parenteral magnesium sulfate injection
Do not administer home sedatives, herbal concoctions, or salt water remedies

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-02] Pre-Eclampsia & Hypertension
CRITERIA: GA >= 20w, BP >= 140/90 mmHg or proteinuria >= 1+.
DANGER SIGNS: Severe frontal headache, vision blur/flashes, epigastric pain, facial edema.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Refer IMMEDIATELY to Level 4 Hospital. Arrange emergency transport. Position on left side.
STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do NOT administer antihypertensives or sedatives. Do NOT attempt Magnesium Sulfate injection at home.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Any vaginal bleeding after 20 weeks gestation is an obstetric emergency. Digital vaginal examination must NEVER be performed by a community health worker or traditional attendant as it can precipitate torrential fatal hemorrhage from placenta previa.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Any vaginal bleeding occurring after 20 weeks gestation.
danger_signs: Painless bright red vaginal bleeding (suspected placenta previa)
Severe continuous abdominal pain with dark bleeding (suspected placental abruption)
Maternal pallor, cold clammy extremities, faintness, rapid weak pulse (hypovolemic shock)
mandated_chw_actions: Arrange IMMEDIATE emergency ambulance/transport to hospital with surgical capacity
Instruct patient to lie strictly on her left side
Keep patient warm and calm
Do not give any solid food or oral fluids in case urgent emergency surgery/anesthesia is needed
negative_boundaries: ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION: NEVER perform digital vaginal examination (PV exam) or allow anyone to examine the cervix
Do not pack the vagina with cloth, cotton, or tampons
Do not give herbal uterine contractions or traditional medicines

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-03] Antepartum Hemorrhage (Bleeding in Late Pregnancy)
CRITERIA: Vaginal bleeding at >= 20 weeks gestation.
DANGER SIGNS: Bright red or dark bleeding, severe uterine pain, pallor, shock.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Immediate emergency hospital transfer. Keep lying on left side. Withhold oral food/drink for surgery.
ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION: NEVER perform digital vaginal exam. Do NOT pack the vagina.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: All pregnant women must take daily Iron and Folic Acid Supplementation (IFAS). Pale palms, conjunctiva, or breathlessness indicates anemia. Severe pallor requires urgent referral for hemoglobin evaluation.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Pregnant woman with pale conjunctiva/palms, fatigue, or known low hemoglobin.
danger_signs: Severe pallor of palms, tongue, and nailbeds
Extreme breathlessness at rest or dizziness upon standing
Swelling of ankles and legs with rapid pulse
mandated_chw_actions: Counsel on strict daily compliance with IFAS (60mg elemental iron / 400mcg folic acid)
Educate on eating iron-rich foods (liver, meat, eggs, beans, dark green leafy vegetables) combined with citrus fruit
If severe pallor is present: refer urgently to health facility for Hb testing and blood transfusion workup
Reassure mother that dark stools are a normal, harmless side-effect of iron tablets
negative_boundaries: Do not advise taking iron tablets with tea, coffee, or milk (tannins and calcium block iron absorption)
Do not manage severe pallor at home with diet alone without hospital referral

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-04] Maternal Anemia & IFAS
CRITERIA: Pale conjunctiva/palms, fatigue, or low Hb.
DANGER SIGNS: Severe pallor, breathlessness at rest, ankle edema.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Daily IFAS compliance (iron + folic acid). Iron-rich diet with vitamin C. Refer severe pallor urgently for Hb test.
PROHIBITED: Do not take iron with tea/coffee/milk. Do not manage severe anemia at home.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.section: Malaria Prevention and Case Management in Pregnancy
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Fever in pregnancy in malaria-endemic zones is an emergency due to risks of miscarriage and maternal death. IPTp-SP must be initiated starting from 13 weeks gestation, given at monthly intervals up to delivery. Bed nets must be used daily.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Pregnant woman presenting with fever (Temp >= 37.5°C) or living in malaria transmission zones.
danger_signs: High fever (>38.5°C) or persistent vomiting
Altered consciousness, convulsions, or extreme lethargy (cerebral malaria)
Jaundice or dark/black urine (hemoglobinuria)
mandated_chw_actions: Perform malaria mRDT if trained and commodities available; otherwise refer immediately for lab testing
Track and support IPTp-SP uptake: ensure 1 dose of Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine (SP) at every scheduled ANC visit from 13 weeks onwards (min 3 doses)
Confirm daily use of Long-Lasting Insecticidal Net (LLIN)
Promptly refer any pregnant woman with fever and positive RDT to health facility for supervised ACT treatment
negative_boundaries: NEVER administer IPTp-SP in the first trimester (<13 weeks gestation)
NEVER administer SP to patients taking daily Cotrimoxazole (Bactrim) prophylaxis (risk of severe antifolate toxicity)
Do not treat fever in pregnancy with simple paracetamol alone without facility evaluation

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-05] Malaria in Pregnancy & IPTp-SP
CRITERIA: Fever (Temp >= 37.5°C) or malaria prevention in pregnancy.
DANGER SIGNS: High fever, vomiting, convulsions, jaundice, dark urine.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Verify daily LLIN use. Track monthly IPTp-SP doses starting at 13 weeks (minimum 3 doses). Refer fever for mRDT and facility treatment.
CONTRAINDICATIONS: NEVER give SP in first trimester (<13w). NEVER give SP if taking Cotrimoxazole.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.section: Danger Signs and Complications of Pregnancy
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Leakage of watery fluid from the birth canal before labor pains begin is premature rupture of membranes. It carries a severe risk of ascending intra-amniotic infection and cord prolapse. Urgent referral is required.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Sudden gush or persistent trickling of clear or colored fluid from vagina without active labor.
danger_signs: Foul-smelling or discolored (greenish/brown) amniotic fluid
Maternal fever (Temp >= 38.0°C) or chills (chorioamnionitis)
Loop of umbilical cord protruding from the vagina (cord prolapse)
Reduced or absent fetal movements
mandated_chw_actions: Refer urgently to health facility with inpatient obstetric capability
Apply a clean dry pad to catch leakage and monitor color and odor
Record the exact time fluid leakage began
If cord prolapse is visible: place mother in knee-chest position immediately and rush to facility
negative_boundaries: ABSOLUTELY FORBIDDEN: Do not perform vaginal examination (introduces lethal pathogens)
Do not advise taking tub baths or washing inside the vagina
Do not administer antibiotics at home

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-06] Premature Rupture of Membranes (PROM)
CRITERIA: Gush or continuous trickling of fluid before labor contractions.
DANGER SIGNS: Foul-smelling/green fluid, maternal fever, cord prolapse, reduced fetal movement.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Urgent facility transfer. Apply clean sanitary pad. Note leakage time. Knee-chest position if cord visible.
FORBIDDEN: Do NOT perform vaginal examination. Do NOT insert anything into vagina.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: By the 28th week of gestation, every pregnant woman must have an agreed Individual Birth Plan documented in MoH 514. This includes chosen health facility, designated transport, emergency savings fund, and designated blood donor.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: All pregnant women at >= 20 weeks gestation.
danger_signs: No birth plan established by 32 weeks gestation
No allocated emergency funds or lack of identified motorized transport
Intention to deliver at home or with traditional birth attendant
mandated_chw_actions: Review and record 5 components of BPCR in MoH 514: 1) Identified health facility; 2) Designated birth companion; 3) Emergency transport driver contact; 4) Emergency savings; 5) Potential compatible blood donor
Ensure essential newborn items are gathered: clean baby clothes, blankets, cap, diapers
Engage husband/partner and household decision-makers to secure financial and logistical agreement
negative_boundaries: Do not support or agree to home delivery plans
Do not rely on walking or wheelbarrows as an emergency transport plan

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-07] Individual Birth Plan (BPCR)
CRITERIA: All pregnant women (finalize by 28-32 weeks).
MANDATED ACTIONS: Complete 5-point birth plan in MoH 514: 1) Facility choice; 2) Birth companion; 3) Emergency transport contact; 4) Savings fund; 5) Potential blood donor. Gather newborn warmth kit.
PROHIBITED: Do not endorse planned home births or unverified transport arrangements.

topic: Labor Signs vs. False Labor & Facility Escort

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.section: Normal Labor, Danger Signs, and Delivery Escort
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: True labor contractions become stronger, longer, and closer together. False labor pains are irregular and fade with walking or resting. CHPs must escort women in true labor to the health facility without delay.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Woman at term (>= 37 weeks) reporting lower abdominal cramping or backache.
danger_signs: Contractions occurring every 2-3 minutes with urge to push (imminent birth)
Bright red bleeding, meconium-stained fluid, or severe unrelenting pain
Labor lasting longer than 12 hours without delivery (prolonged labor)
mandated_chw_actions: Differentiate true labor (regular, tightening, increasing frequency/intensity, bloody show) from false labor (irregular, relieved by rest)
If true labor confirmed: immediately call designated transport and escort woman to facility
Carry maternal health booklet (MoH 216) and emergency contact details
Encourage calm breathing and supportive positioning during travel
negative_boundaries: Do not wait until the head is crowning to initiate travel
STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not administer traditional labor-accelerating herbs ('kaloba' / uterine stimulants)
Do not advise prolonged pushing before reaching the health facility

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-08] Labor Signs & Facility Escort
CRITERIA: Gestation >= 37 weeks with labor contractions.
DANGER SIGNS: Contractions every 2-3 min, urge to push, vaginal bleeding, labor >12 hours.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Verify true labor (regular contractions, bloody show). Immediately activate transport and escort to facility with MoH 216 card.
PROHIBITED: Never give traditional labor herbs. Do not delay facility transfer.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.section: Emergency Delivery Triage in Community Settings
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: If delivery is imminent and transfer is impossible, ensure clean hands and surfaces. Support the baby's head gently without pulling. Place baby skin-to-skin immediately. Never pull the umbilical cord to deliver the placenta.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Baby's head visible at vaginal opening (crowning); impossible to reach facility in time.
danger_signs: Loop of umbilical cord prolapsed ahead of head
Hand, foot, or breech presentation (malpresentation)
Retained placenta (>30 minutes after baby's birth) or severe bleeding
mandated_chw_actions: Wash hands thoroughly with soap and clean running water; spread clean dry cloth under mother
Support head gently as it delivers; do not pull baby
Immediately wipe baby's face, dry body thoroughly, and place skin-to-skin on mother's bare chest; cover with warm dry cloth and cap
Wait 1-3 minutes before tying cord with two clean ties (at 2cm and 5cm from abdomen) and cut with sterile blade
Encourage immediate breastfeeding; massage fundus gently after placenta delivers spontaneously
Arrange immediate post-delivery transfer of mother-baby dyad to health facility
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: NEVER pull on the umbilical cord to speed delivery of placenta (causes fatal uterine inversion)
NEVER insert fingers or hands into the birth canal
Do not bathe the baby for at least 24 hours

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-09] Imminent Emergency Delivery
CRITERIA: Head crowning; delivery unavoidable before transport.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Clean hands. Support head gently (no pulling). Dry baby immediately. Skin-to-skin on mother's chest. Tie cord at 2cm and 5cm with clean ties. Cut with sterile blade. Immediate breastfeeding. Escort dyad to facility.
ABSOLUTELY FORBIDDEN: NEVER pull the cord to deliver placenta. Never insert hands into birth canal.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: The first 48 hours after birth carry the highest risk of maternal and neonatal death. CHPs must visit the mother and baby within 24 hours of birth, followed by visits on Day 3 (48-72h), Day 7-14, and at 6 weeks.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: All recently delivered mothers and newborns in the community unit.
danger_signs: No PNC contact within first 48 hours after delivery
Fever, heavy bleeding, or newborn inability to feed at any visit
mandated_chw_actions: Conduct 4 scheduled home PNC visits: Visit 1 (<24h), Visit 2 (Day 3 / 48-72h), Visit 3 (Day 7-14), Visit 4 (6 weeks)
Assess maternal vitals, uterine involution, vaginal bleeding (lochia), and emotional well-being
Assess newborn cord healing, temperature, breathing rate, color, and breastfeeding latch
Verify birth registration and confirm BCG and OPV0 immunization uptake
negative_boundaries: Do not delay the first visit beyond 48 hours post-delivery
Do not discharge a mother-baby dyad from active monitoring if danger signs are present

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-10] Postnatal Care (PNC) Schedule
CRITERIA: All recently delivered mothers and newborns.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Conduct 4 PNC visits: Visit 1 (<24h), Visit 2 (Day 3), Visit 3 (Day 7-14), Visit 4 (6 weeks). Check maternal bleeding, fever, depression; check newborn cord, breathing, temperature, and breastfeeding.
RULE: Never delay the first PNC visit beyond 48 hours.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Severe bleeding after delivery (soaking more than two sanitary pads in an hour or continuous trickle) is postpartum hemorrhage. It is the leading cause of maternal mortality. Continuous fundal massage and immediate emergency referral are required.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Woman who has delivered within the past 6 weeks soaking >2 large pads in 1 hour or passing large clots.
danger_signs: Continuous trickling or gushing of blood from vagina
Soft, boggy uterus that does not harden on palpation
Maternal pallor, cold extremities, rapid weak pulse, dizziness, or loss of consciousness
mandated_chw_actions: ACT IMMEDIATELY: Call emergency transport for transfer to hospital with blood transfusion and surgical capacity
Perform vigorous, circular uterine fundal massage until uterus contracts into a firm, hard ball
Put newborn to breast immediately (suckling stimulates natural oxytocin release and uterine contraction)
Keep mother lying flat with legs elevated 30 cm; keep warm with blankets; do not leave unattended
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: NEVER pack the vagina with cloth, cotton, or towels (conceals internal bleeding)
NEVER give herbal remedies or sedatives
Do not stop fundal massage until uterus is firm and transfer arrives

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-11] Postpartum Hemorrhage (PPH)
CRITERIA: Soaking >2 pads in 1 hour, continuous bleeding, or boggy uterus.
DANGER SIGNS: Gushing blood, dizziness, pallor, rapid pulse, loss of consciousness.
MANDATED ACTIONS: EMERGENCY transfer to Level 4 Hospital. Vigorously massage uterine fundus until firm. Put baby to breast immediately. Elevate legs, keep warm.
ABSOLUTELY FORBIDDEN: Never pack vagina with cloth. Do not give herbal concoctions.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Fever greater than 38°C occurring between delivery and 42 days postpartum, accompanied by foul-smelling vaginal discharge and pelvic pain, is puerperal sepsis. It requires urgent hospital referral for systemic intravenous antibiotics.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Woman within 42 days of delivery presenting with fever (Temp >= 38.0°C) or foul lochia.
danger_signs: Foul-smelling, purulent vaginal discharge (lochia)
Severe continuous lower abdominal or uterine tenderness
High fever with rigors, sweating, and rapid breathing
Lethargy, confusion, or drop in blood pressure (septic shock)
mandated_chw_actions: Refer urgently to Level 4 Health Facility for clinical workup and intravenous antibiotic therapy
Encourage clean fluid intake to prevent dehydration
Instruct on hygiene: change clean pads frequently; wash hands before and after perineal care
Help arrange transport and child care for older siblings
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not treat with oral paracetamol alone without facility referral
STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not douch, wash inside the vagina, or insert herbal pessaries
Do not delay referral beyond 4 hours

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-12] Puerperal Sepsis (Postpartum Infection)
CRITERIA: Postpartum fever (Temp >= 38.0°C) or foul vaginal discharge within 6 weeks.
DANGER SIGNS: Foul-smelling lochia, severe lower abdominal tenderness, chills, septic shock.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Urgent referral to Level 4 Hospital for IV antibiotics. Encourage hydration. Strict hand hygiene.
FORBIDDEN: Do not treat with simple analgesics alone. NEVER douche or wash inside vagina.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in the Postnatal Period
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Postpartum depression and psychosis can occur within the first year after delivery. Severe depression, withdrawal, or thoughts of self-harm or harming the infant require immediate medical and psychiatric assessment.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Postpartum mother exhibiting persistent low mood, loss of interest, severe anxiety, or detachment from newborn.
danger_signs: Mother expressing thoughts of suicide or self-harm
Mother expressing thoughts or urges to harm the newborn
Disorganized speech, hearing voices, extreme agitation, or confusion (postpartum psychosis)
Complete refusal to feed, touch, or care for the newborn
mandated_chw_actions: Provide empathetic, non-judgmental listening; reassure mother that depression is a treatable medical condition, not a personal failure
Engage spouse, mother-in-law, or trusted family members to take over newborn care and household duties
If self-harm or psychosis signs are present: arrange IMMEDIATE escorted facility transfer to medical/psychiatric team
Ensure the infant is never left alone unsupervised with the mother if severe detachment or psychosis is suspected
negative_boundaries: Do not dismiss symptoms as 'spiritual weakness', 'demonic possession', or laziness
Do not recommend isolation or physical restraint at home

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-13] Maternal Postpartum Mental Health
CRITERIA: Persistent sadness, crying, severe anxiety, or detachment within 1 year of birth.
DANGER SIGNS: Thoughts of self-harm or harming baby, hallucinations, hearing voices, refusal to care for infant.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Empathetic counseling. Mobilize family support for infant care. Immediate escorted referral for psychiatric evaluation if self-harm/psychosis suspected. Keep infant supervised.
PROHIBITED: Do not dismiss as spiritual weakness. Never leave infant unmonitored.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Newborn hypothermia is a silent killer. Immediate drying, direct skin-to-skin contact with the mother, and delayed bathing for at least 24 hours are vital protective interventions.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: All newborns from delivery through the first 28 days of life.
danger_signs: Axillary temperature < 36.5°C (hypothermia) or cold extremities with blue lips
Baby cold to touch, sluggish, weak cry, and refusing to breastfeed
Body temperature > 37.5°C (hyperthermia or fever)
mandated_chw_actions: Immediately place newborn naked (with diaper and cap) skin-to-skin on mother's bare chest; cover both with warm dry blanket
Keep room warm (>25°C), closed, and protected from drafts
Ensure baby wears a warm hat and socks; change wet diapers immediately
Promote frequent breastfeeding every 2 hours to provide calories for thermoregulation
If temp remains < 36.5°C despite 1 hour of skin-to-skin: refer urgently to health facility
negative_boundaries: ABSOLUTELY FORBIDDEN: Do not bathe the newborn within the first 24 hours of life
NEVER use hot water bottles, charcoal jikos, or open flames near the baby (severe risk of burns and carbon monoxide poisoning)
Do not leave newborn unwrapped on cold scales or tables

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-14] Newborn Thermal Care & Hypothermia
CRITERIA: All newborns (0-28 days).
DANGER SIGNS: Axillary temp < 36.5°C, cold extremities, weak suckling, blue lips, temp > 37.5°C.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Immediate skin-to-skin contact on mother's chest. Warm hat, socks, blanket. Breastfeed every 2 hours. Refer if cold persists after 1 hour.
FORBIDDEN: Do NOT bathe within first 24 hours. NEVER use hot water bottles or charcoal jikos near baby.

topic: Cord Care with 7.1% Chlorhexidine Digluconate Gel

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.section: Clean Cord Care and Infection Prevention
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Apply 7.1% Chlorhexidine digluconate gel to the cord stump and surrounding skin daily for the first 7 days of life. Never apply cow dung, ash, soot, cooking oil, or traditional powders to the cord.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: All newborns from birth until the umbilical cord stump separates and heals.
danger_signs: Application of animal dung, mud, ash, or unprescribed powders to the cord
Bleeding from the cord tie or cut surface
mandated_chw_actions: Teach mother clean handwashing with soap and clean water before touching the cord
Demonstrate application of 7.1% Chlorhexidine digluconate gel (delivering 4% chlorhexidine) to the cord stump, base, and around umbilicus once daily for 7 days
Keep the cord stump clean, exposed to air, and loosely covered with clean loose clothing
Fold the diaper below the umbilicus to avoid urine contamination
negative_boundaries: ABSOLUTE PROHIBITION: Do NOT apply cow dung, mud, ash, soot, saliva, breast milk, or herbal pastes to the cord
Do NOT bandage, bind, or seal the cord stump with coins or tight cloth wraps
Do not pull on the cord stump even if it is hanging by a thread

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-15] Cord Care & 7.1% Chlorhexidine
CRITERIA: Daily cord care for all newborns until healed.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Wash hands with soap. Apply 7.1% Chlorhexidine gel to cord stump and base once daily for 7 days. Keep exposed to air. Fold diaper below umbilicus.
STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: NEVER apply cow dung, ash, oil, saliva, or herbs. Do NOT bandage tightly or pull stump.

topic: Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) for Low Birth Weight (<2.5 kg)

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.section: Care of the Small and Low Birth Weight Newborn
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Babies born weighing less than 2,500g or born before 37 weeks require Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC). Continuous skin-to-skin contact, frequent feeding, and infection control dramatically increase survival.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Stable newborn with birth weight < 2,500g (2.5 kg) or born before 37 completed weeks.
danger_signs: Weight < 2,000g (< 2.0 kg) or inability to suckle from breast
Apneic pauses (baby stops breathing for >20 seconds or turns blue)
Persistent hypothermia (< 36.5°C) despite KMC
Loss of >10% of birth weight
mandated_chw_actions: Teach and support continuous Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC): position infant naked (cap and diaper only) upright on mother's bare chest between breasts
Secure baby with KMC binder or soft wrap; engage father or relatives to share KMC shifts
Support frequent exclusive breastfeeding or cup feeding with expressed breast milk every 2 hours
Weigh baby weekly using CHP hanging scale and track growth trajectory
Refer promptly if breathing difficulty, severe lethargy, or weight loss occurs
negative_boundaries: Do not isolate low birth weight baby in separate crib away from mother
Do not feed animal milk, infant formula, or tea
Do not use hot water bottles or warm stones

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-16] Kangaroo Mother Care (Low Birth Weight <2.5kg)
CRITERIA: Stable infant birth weight < 2,500g or preterm.
DANGER SIGNS: Weight < 2,000g, breathing pauses >20s, inability to feed, persistent hypothermia.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Continuous skin-to-skin KMC in upright chest position. Warm cap and wrap. Feed expressed milk/breastfeed every 2 hours. Weekly weight tracking.
PROHIBITED: Do not isolate baby from mother. Never give non-breastmilk liquids.

topic: Severe Neonatal Sepsis / Systemic Infection Triage

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.section: Management of Sick Newborn and Referral Danger Signs
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Any newborn with danger signs including inability to feed, convulsions, fast breathing (>60 breaths/min), severe chest indrawing, or fever/hypothermia has severe neonatal infection and requires immediate emergency hospital admission.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Newborn (0-28 days) presenting with any general danger sign of severe illness.
danger_signs: Inability to suckle, latch, or feed at all
Convulsions, fits, or abnormal twitching of limbs
Fast breathing (respiratory rate >= 60 breaths/min on two counts)
Severe lower chest wall indrawing (deep hollows on inhalation)
Grunting on exhalation or cyanosis (blue tongue/lips)
Abnormally sleepy, lethargic, or unconscious; floppy posture
Fever (Temp > 37.5°C) or severe hypothermia (< 36.5°C not correcting)
mandated_chw_actions: MEDICAL EMERGENCY: Facilitate IMMEDIATE emergency hospital transfer to Level 4/Newborn Unit
Instruct mother to carry baby skin-to-skin under her clothing to maintain warmth during transit
If baby is able to swallow: encourage frequent sips of expressed breast milk on the way
Alert receiving facility staff in advance if communication is available
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not administer oral or injectable antibiotics at home (must be given at hospital)
STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not give cold water sponge baths to febrile newborns
Do not force-feed a convulsing or unconscious infant (risk of fatal aspiration)

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-17] Severe Neonatal Sepsis (Danger Signs)
CRITERIA: Newborn 0-28 days with systemic danger signs.
DANGER SIGNS: Inability to feed, convulsions, fast breathing >= 60/min, chest indrawing, grunting, lethargy, fever/hypothermia.
MANDATED ACTIONS: MEDICAL EMERGENCY. Immediate transfer to hospital newborn unit. Keep skin-to-skin warm during transit. Sips of breast milk if swallowing.
FORBIDDEN: Do NOT give antibiotics at home. Never force-feed a convulsing/unconscious baby.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Redness extending onto the skin of the abdomen around the umbilicus, accompanied by pus or foul odor, is omphalitis. Because infection can rapidly spread internally to the peritoneum and liver, immediate hospital referral is mandatory.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Newborn presenting with umbilical redness, swelling, or purulent discharge.
danger_signs: Redness extending onto the abdominal skin around the base (>1 cm)
Pus oozing from the cord stump with foul odor
Baby crying when the area around the umbilicus is gently touched
Accompanied by fever (Temp > 37.5°C), lethargy, or poor feeding
mandated_chw_actions: Refer IMMEDIATELY to Level 3/4 health facility for systemic antibiotic evaluation
Wash hands with soap and water; gently clean surface pus with sterile water and apply 7.1% Chlorhexidine gel
Counsel mother to keep the area clean and exposed; fold diaper down
Counsel family against traditional remedies; explain the risk of blood infection (sepsis)
negative_boundaries: ABSOLUTELY FORBIDDEN: Do NOT apply cow dung, ash, herbal pastes, or cooking oil
Do NOT squeeze, puncture, or cut the inflamed cord base
Do not bandage or seal with adhesive tape

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-18] Omphalitis (Severe Cord Infection)
CRITERIA: Umbilical redness spreading to abdominal skin, pus, or foul odor.
DANGER SIGNS: Redness >1cm around cord, pus, tenderness, fever, lethargy.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Refer IMMEDIATELY to hospital for systemic antibiotics. Clean with clean water and apply 7.1% chlorhexidine. Counsel family against harmful traditional concoctions.
PROHIBITED: Never apply cow dung, ash, or herbs. Do NOT squeeze or bandage.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.section: Jaundice and Bilirubin Assessment in the Newborn
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Jaundice appearing on the first day of life, or deep jaundice extending to the palms and soles at any time, is pathological. Untreated severe jaundice causes irreversible brain damage (kernicterus). Urgent referral for phototherapy is required.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Newborn exhibiting yellowish discoloration of the whites of eyes, face, trunk, or extremities.
danger_signs: Jaundice appearing within the first 24 hours of birth (always pathological)
Deep yellow palms and soles of the feet at any age
Dark urine or pale/clay-colored stools
Baby unusually sleepy, difficult to wake, arching back, or crying with high-pitched sound (kernicterus warning)
mandated_chw_actions: Refer urgently to health facility with laboratory bilirubin testing and phototherapy equipment
Encourage frequent exclusive breastfeeding (every 1.5 to 2 hours) to promote bowel movements and bilirubin excretion
Instruct family not to delay referral; explain brain toxicity risk
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not advise exposing the baby to direct burning sunlight (causes severe sunburn and dehydration without curing pathological jaundice)
Do not give glucose water, herbal concoctions, or formula feeds
Do not delay referral for jaundice extending to feet

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-19] Neonatal Jaundice
CRITERIA: Yellow skin/eyes in newborn.
DANGER SIGNS: Jaundice in first 24 hours of life; yellow palms and soles; dark urine/pale stool; high-pitched cry/lethargy.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Urgent hospital referral for phototherapy/bilirubin testing. Feed frequently (every 2 hours) to clear bilirubin.
FORBIDDEN: Do NOT place in direct burning sunlight. Never give glucose water or herbal tea.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.section: Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) in Community Health
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Initiate breastfeeding within the first hour of life. Practice exclusive breastfeeding for 6 months. Colostrum is the baby's first immunization. Prelacteal feeds such as water, sugar water, honey, or butter are strictly prohibited.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: All newborns and infants up to 6 months of age.
danger_signs: Baby unable to attach or maintain latch at breast
Mother experiencing severely cracked, bleeding, or infected nipples (mastitis)
Mother reporting giving prelacteal feeds (water, sugar water, tea, honey, animal milk)
mandated_chw_actions: Ensure initiation within 1st hour of life; ensure newborn receives golden colostrum
Assess and guide 4 signs of good attachment: 1) Mouth wide open; 2) Lower lip curled outward; 3) Chin touching breast; 4) More areola visible above than below mouth
Promote on-demand exclusive breastfeeding (at least 8-12 times in 24 hours, day and night)
Reassure mother that breast milk contains all needed water, even in hot weather
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do NOT give prelacteal feeds (water, sugar water, honey, butter, animal milk, tea) — destroys gut barrier and causes lethal diarrhea
Do not discard colostrum
Do not use pacifiers, artificial teats, or feeding bottles

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-20] Exclusive Breastfeeding & Latch
CRITERIA: All infants 0-6 months.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Initiate within 1 hour. Feed colostrum. Ensure good attachment (mouth wide open, lower lip outward, chin on breast). Feed on demand 8-12 times/day. Give ONLY breastmilk for 6 months.
STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: NO prelacteal feeds (no water, sugar, honey, tea, butter, animal milk). No bottles or pacifiers.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 1: Household Health Promotion
source_reference.section: Safe Water Storage and Treatment (eCHIS WASH-01)
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: All drinking water must be treated at the household level using an approved method: rolling boil for at least 1 minute, chlorination using WaterGuard or Aquatabs (1 cap per 20L jerrycan, wait 30 minutes), or certified ceramic candle filtration. Water must be stored in a clean container with a narrow mouth and secure lid.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Any household using unpiped, surface, well, or questionable water sources for drinking and food preparation.
danger_signs: Turbid untreated water used directly for infant formula or drinking
Wide-mouth storage pots without lid where hands touch water
mandated_chw_actions: Assess current water source and demonstrate correct WaterGuard dosing: 1 cap per 20 litres of clear water (2 caps if turbid after straining)
Wait 30 minutes after chlorination before drinking
Ensure boiling achieves a vigorous rolling boil for at least 1 full minute
Promote narrow-neck jerrycans with taps or screw caps to prevent hand recontamination
negative_boundaries: Do not add chemical coagulants without precise measuring tools
Do not store treated water in open buckets or dip cups into storage container
Do not assume river or shallow well water is safe even if clear without treatment

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-WASH-01] Household Water Treatment
CRITERIA: Household using untreated or questionable drinking water.
ACTIONS: Demonstrate treatment: 1 cap WaterGuard per 20L jerrycan (wait 30 mins) OR rolling boil for 1 full minute. Store in clean, narrow-neck covered container.
PROHIBITED: Do not store in open-mouth basins. Do not dip cups directly into drinking water.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 1: Household Health Promotion
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Every household must have access to a clean, functional latrine located at least 15 meters from any water source. A handwashing station (leaky tin / tippy-tap) equipped with soap and running water must be stationed immediately outside the latrine. Hands must be washed at the 5 critical times.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: All households during routine MoH 514 environmental mapping and child health visits.
danger_signs: Open defecation around compound
Absence of soap or running water near latrine
Latrine located within 15 meters of dug well or river
mandated_chw_actions: Inspect latrine slab, drop-hole cover, and superstructure for cleanliness and fly-proofing
Construct and maintain functional leaky tin / tippy-tap handwashing facility outside latrine
Counsel on 5 critical handwashing moments: after toilet, after cleaning baby's bottom, before preparing food, before feeding child, before eating
negative_boundaries: Do not permit washing hands in a shared basin of stagnant water
Do not use ash as a permanent replacement for soap if soap is obtainable
Do not allow open defecation even for young children (dispose infant feces in latrine)

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-WASH-02] Sanitation & Handwashing Stations
CRITERIA: Household sanitation inspection.
ACTIONS: Verify latrine hygiene (>15m from water source). Ensure functional tippy-tap with soap and running water outside latrine. Enforce 5 critical handwashing moments.
PROHIBITED: Do not wash hands in communal standing basin. Do not leave infant feces uncovered.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 1: Household Health Promotion
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Community Health Promoters must ensure universal coverage of Long-Lasting Insecticidal Nets (LLINs) in all endemic and epidemic-prone zones. Every sleeping space must be covered. Stagnant water collections around compounds must be drained or backfilled to eliminate mosquito breeding sites.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Households in malaria-endemic lake and coastal regions, or epidemic-prone highland areas.
danger_signs: Torn, uninspected bednets with holes
Stagnant pools of water within 100 meters of sleeping huts
Pregnant women or under-5s sleeping without nets
mandated_chw_actions: Verify that every bed and sleeping mat has a functional LLIN properly tucked under mattress
Organize community clean-up to clear bushes and drain standing water bodies
Prioritize net allocation to pregnant women and children under 5 years
negative_boundaries: Do not wash LLINs in natural water bodies (rivers, lakes) as insecticide is toxic to aquatic life
Do not dry nets in direct scorching sun (degrades permethrin/deltamethrin efficacy)
Do not use insecticide nets for fishing, poultry fencing, or crop protection

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-WASH-03] Vector Control & LLIN Bednets
CRITERIA: Household vector and malaria risk screening.
ACTIONS: Ensure 1 LLIN per sleeping space, tucked in. Prioritize pregnant women and under-5s. Drain standing water around compound.
PROHIBITED: Never wash nets in rivers or lakes. Do not repurpose bednets for fishing or farming.

topic: General Danger Signs in Sick Children (2m–5y)

source_reference.manual: Integrated Community Case Management (iCCM) Technical Manual
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Before evaluating specific symptoms, every CHP must check for the four universal general danger signs: 1) Unable to drink or breastfeed, 2) Vomits everything, 3) Convulsions during this illness, 4) Lethargic or unconscious. Presence of ANY general danger sign requires immediate emergency referral to a health facility.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Any child aged 2 months to 5 years presenting with acute fever, cough, diarrhea, or lethargy.
danger_signs: Unable to drink or suckle breast
Vomiting everything consumed
History of convulsions / fits during present illness
Abnormally sleepy, difficult to wake, or completely unconscious
mandated_chw_actions: Declare immediate medical emergency and mobilize urgent transport to nearest Level 4 facility
Keep child warm during transit (skin-to-skin or warm dry blankets)
If child is conscious and able to swallow, offer frequent small sips of clean water or breastmilk to prevent hypoglycemia
Alert receiving facility via eCHIS emergency referral slip (MoH 515)
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not attempt to give oral medications or fluids to an unconscious or actively convulsing child
Do not delay referral to administer oral antibiotics or antimalarials
Do not recommend herbal infusions or traditional body scarification

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-ICCM-01] General Danger Signs in Under-5s
CRITERIA: Child 2-59m with acute illness.
DANGER SIGNS: 1) Unable to drink/suckle, 2) Vomits everything, 3) Convulsions, 4) Lethargic/unconscious.
ACTIONS: Immediate emergency transfer to hospital. Keep warm. Notify facility with MoH 515.
PROHIBITED: Never force oral fluids/drugs on an unconscious or convulsing child. Do not delay referral.

topic: Uncomplicated Malaria: mRDT Testing & AL Dosing

source_reference.manual: Integrated Community Case Management (iCCM) Technical Manual
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Any child aged 2 months to 5 years with fever or history of fever must be tested with a malaria rapid diagnostic test (mRDT). If mRDT is positive and no general danger signs are present, treat with Artemether-Lumefantrine (AL) according to weight/age. First dose must be directly observed by the CHP.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Child 2–59 months with fever (axillary temp >= 37.5 C) or reported fever in last 48 hours, mRDT positive, NO danger signs.
danger_signs: Lethargy, convulsions, inability to drink, persistent vomiting (signs of severe malaria)
Jaundice (yellow eyes/palms), severe pallor, dark cola-colored urine
mandated_chw_actions: Perform finger-prick mRDT using aseptic technique and read at 15 minutes
If mRDT Positive, dispense Artemether-Lumefantrine (AL):
- Weight 5 to <15 kg (approx 2–35 months): Yellow blister pack, 1 tab twice daily for 3 days (6 tabs total)
- Weight 15 to <25 kg (approx 3–5 years): Blue blister pack, 2 tabs twice daily for 3 days (12 tabs total)
Directly observe 1st dose; instruct caregiver to give with milk or fatty meal for absorption
Re-treat with full dose if child vomits within 30 minutes of swallowing
Follow up at home on Day 3 to verify adherence and fever resolution
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not give AL if mRDT is negative (refer for non-malarial fever workup)
Do not give adult AL formulations or break random adult tablets
Do not dispense oral artemisinin monotherapy or quinine injections at community level

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-ICCM-02] Uncomplicated Malaria (mRDT+ & AL)
CRITERIA: Child 2-59m, fever, mRDT positive, no danger signs.
ACTIONS: Give Artemether-Lumefantrine (AL) twice daily for 3 days (Yellow pack 5-<15kg: 1 tab bd; Blue pack 15-<25kg: 2 tabs bd). Take with fatty food/milk. Directly observe dose 1. Follow up Day 3.
PROHIBITED: Never treat if mRDT is negative. No adult tablets.

source_reference.manual: National Guidelines for the Diagnosis, Treatment and Prevention of Malaria in Kenya
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: When a child under 6 years presents with suspected severe malaria (fever with any danger sign: convulsions, coma, prostration, inability to swallow) and cannot take oral medications, the CHP must administer a single dose of rectal artesunate (100mg suppository) as pre-referral treatment and refer immediately.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Child aged 2 months to <6 years with confirmed or suspected malaria presenting with one or more general danger signs.
danger_signs: Multiple convulsions within 24 hours
Coma / unarousable unconsciousness
Extreme prostration (cannot sit up or support head)
Respiratory distress / deep acidotic breathing
mandated_chw_actions: Insert single Rectal Artesunate Suppository (100mg) into rectum; hold buttocks together for 10 minutes to prevent expulsion
If expelled within 30 minutes, insert a replacement suppository
Initiate immediate emergency transfer to nearest CEmoNC / Level 4 facility for IV artesunate
Document dose on MoH 515 referral slip with exact administration timestamp
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not administer repeated doses of rectal artesunate (it is strictly a single pre-referral intervention)
Do not attempt to give oral AL or oral fluids to a convulsing or comatose child
Do not delay ambulance transfer to wait for clinical improvement

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-ICCM-03] Severe Malaria Pre-Referral (RAS)
CRITERIA: Child <6y with fever and danger signs (coma, convulsions, prostration).
ACTIONS: Administer 1 Rectal Artesunate Suppository (100mg). Hold buttocks 10 mins. Immediate emergency transfer to hospital. Record time on MoH 515.
PROHIBITED: Never repeat suppository dose. Do not give oral medication. Do not delay referral.

topic: Pediatric Pneumonia: Fast Breathing & Amoxicillin DT

source_reference.manual: Integrated Community Case Management (iCCM) Technical Manual
source_reference.section: Management of Cough and Fast Breathing
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: A child with cough or difficulty breathing must have breaths counted for a full 60 seconds when calm. Fast breathing is defined as: 50 breaths per minute or more for age 2-11 months; 40 breaths per minute or more for age 12-59 months. If fast breathing is present without chest indrawing or stridor, treat with dispersible Amoxicillin DT 250mg for 5 days.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Child 2–59 months with cough or labored breathing, elevated respiratory rate by age, and NO chest indrawing or stridor.
danger_signs: Chest wall indrawing (subcostal retractions)
Stridor when calm, grunting, or nasal flaring
Central cyanosis (blue lips or tongue)
mandated_chw_actions: Count breaths for 60 full seconds using timer while child is calm and not crying
Confirm threshold: Age 2-11m: >=50 bpm; Age 12-59m: >=40 bpm
Dispense Amoxicillin Dispersible Tablets (DT) 250mg twice daily for 5 days:
- Age 2 to 11 months: 1 tablet twice daily for 5 days (10 tablets total)
- Age 12 to 59 months: 2 tablets twice daily for 5 days (20 tablets total)
Demonstrate dissolving tablet in 5ml clean water/breastmilk; observe first dose
Advise caregiver on soothing throat with safe warm fluids and follow-up on Day 3
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not dispense adult capsules, co-trimoxazole, or erythromycin
Do not recommend commercial cough syrups, throat lozenges, or cold decongestants (unsafe under 5)
Do not delay referral if chest indrawing or stridor is present

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-ICCM-04] Fast Breathing Pneumonia (Amoxicillin DT)
CRITERIA: Child 2-59m with cough and fast breathing (2-11m: >=50 bpm; 12-59m: >=40 bpm), no indrawing.
ACTIONS: Amoxicillin DT 250mg twice daily for 5 days (2-11m: 1 tab bd; 12-59m: 2 tabs bd). Disperse in water. Directly observe dose 1. Follow up Day 3.
PROHIBITED: No cough syrups or cold meds. Do not treat if chest indrawing present (refer).

topic: Severe Pneumonia: Chest Indrawing & Stridor Referral

source_reference.manual: Integrated Community Case Management (iCCM) Technical Manual
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Any child with cough or difficulty breathing accompanied by chest indrawing (lower chest wall moves in when child breathes in) or stridor in a calm child has severe pneumonia and must be referred urgently to a hospital. CHPs must not attempt home treatment.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Child 2–59 months with cough/difficulty breathing and chest indrawing or stridor.
danger_signs: Deep subcostal lower chest indrawing
Harsh stridor sound on inspiration when child is rested and calm
Grunting respirations with head nodding
mandated_chw_actions: Give first pre-referral dose of Amoxicillin DT if available and child can swallow
Keep child in comfortable upright position and warm during transfer
Immediate emergency referral to Level 4 hospital with oxygen capacity
Complete MoH 515 referral tracking slip
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not keep child at home on oral treatment alone
Do not attempt steam inhalation with boiling pots (high pediatric burn hazard)
Do not administer sedatives to quiet breathing struggle

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-ICCM-05] Severe Pneumonia & Chest Indrawing
CRITERIA: Child 2-59m with cough and chest indrawing or stridor.
ACTIONS: Give 1 pre-referral dose Amoxicillin DT if swallowable. Immediate emergency transfer to hospital with oxygen. Keep upright.
PROHIBITED: Never treat at home. Do not give sedatives or boiling steam tents.

topic: Acute Diarrhea: Low-Osmolarity ORS & Zinc Sulfate

source_reference.manual: Integrated Community Case Management (iCCM) Technical Manual
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Diarrhea is defined as 3 or more loose or watery stools in 24 hours. Every child with acute diarrhea without severe dehydration must be treated with low-osmolarity Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) and Zinc Sulfate 20mg dispersible tablets for a full 14 days to reduce duration and prevent future episodes.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Child 2–59 months with >=3 loose watery stools in past 24 hours, alert, drinking eagerly, NO blood in stool.
danger_signs: Sunken eyes, skin pinch takes >2 seconds, unable to drink (severe dehydration)
Blood visible in stool (dysentery)
High fever and repeated vomiting
mandated_chw_actions: Demonstrate mixing 1 sachet low-osmolarity ORS in exactly 1 litre of clean drinking water
Administer ORS after every loose stool: 50-100ml for under 2 years; 100-200ml for 2 years and above
Dispense Zinc Sulfate dispersible tablets (daily for 14 full days):
- Age 2 to 6 months: 10mg (half tablet) daily for 14 days
- Age 6 to 59 months: 20mg (one full tablet) daily for 14 days
Counsel to continue frequent breastfeeding and regular nutritious meals
Follow-up visit at home on Day 3
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not administer anti-diarrheal drugs (no loperamide, diphenoxylate)
Do not mix ORS in less or more than exactly 1 litre of water (dangerous electrolyte imbalance)
Do not discontinue Zinc when diarrhea stops before completing 14 days

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-ICCM-06] Diarrhea Treatment (ORS + Zinc)
CRITERIA: Child 2-59m with >=3 loose stools in 24h, alert, drinking.
ACTIONS: Mix 1 ORS sachet in exactly 1L clean water; give after each stool. Give Zinc Sulfate for 14 full days (2-6m: 10mg daily; 6-59m: 20mg daily). Continue feeding.
PROHIBITED: Never give anti-diarrheals (loperamide). Do not stop zinc early. Do not mix ORS in wrong volume.

source_reference.manual: Integrated Community Case Management (iCCM) Technical Manual
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: A child with diarrhea who has two or more of: 1) Lethargy or unconsciousness, 2) Sunken eyes, 3) Unable to drink or drinking poorly, 4) Skin pinch going back very slowly (>2 seconds), has severe dehydration. This is a life-threatening medical emergency requiring immediate IV fluid resuscitation.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Child with diarrhea and at least 2 signs of severe dehydration: lethargic/unconscious, sunken eyes, unable to drink, skin pinch >2s.
danger_signs: Unconsciousness, cold clammy extremities, feeble impalpable pulse (hypovolemic shock)
Skin pinch on abdomen takes >2 seconds to flatten
Deep rapid breathing (metabolic acidosis)
mandated_chw_actions: Call for immediate emergency transport to facility with intravenous fluid capacity
If child is conscious and can swallow, offer frequent sips of ORS during transport
Keep child warm and secure; notify health center via MoH 515 referral form
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not attempt to force oral fluids into an unconscious child (aspiration hazard)
Do not attempt to start IV cannulation at home unless formally licensed
Do not give anti-emetics or adult glucose drips orally

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-ICCM-07] Severe Dehydration Emergency
CRITERIA: Child with diarrhea + 2 signs: lethargic/unconscious, sunken eyes, skin pinch >2s, unable to drink.
ACTIONS: Immediate emergency transfer to hospital for IV fluids. Give ORS sips only if conscious. Keep warm.
PROHIBITED: Never force fluids on an unconscious child. Do not delay for home remedies.

source_reference.manual: Integrated Community Case Management (iCCM) Technical Manual
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Any child with diarrhea who has visible red blood in their stool has dysentery (shigellosis until proven otherwise). Dysentery causes rapid bowel wall necrosis and high mortality in malnourished children. CHPs must begin ORS and refer immediately for targeted antibiotic treatment.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Caregiver reports or CHP observes visible red blood in loose or watery stools.
danger_signs: High fever with toxic appearance
Severe abdominal distension or peritoneal tenderness
Co-occurring severe acute malnutrition
mandated_chw_actions: Initiate ORS fluid replenishment to prevent concurrent dehydration
Start Zinc Sulfate 20mg supplementation
Urgent referral to dispensary/health center for clinical assessment and targeted antibiotic (Ciprofloxacin)
Educate household on fly control, latrine disinfection, and handwashing
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not administer antispasmodics, kaolin, or loperamide (traps toxins in bowel)
Do not administer deworming tablets as a treatment for acute bloody diarrhea
Do not withhold food or fluids

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-ICCM-08] Dysentery (Bloody Diarrhea)
CRITERIA: Child 2-59m with visible blood in stool.
ACTIONS: Start ORS and Zinc Sulfate. Refer urgently to health facility for targeted antibiotic (Ciprofloxacin). Enforce handwashing and latrine hygiene.
PROHIBITED: Never give anti-motility drugs (loperamide). Do not treat with dewormers.

topic: Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) & Bilateral Pitting Edema

source_reference.manual: National Guideline for Integrated Management of Acute Malnutrition (IMAM)
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: All children aged 6 to 59 months must have their nutritional status assessed using Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) and checking for bilateral pitting edema of the feet. A MUAC less than 11.5 cm (red color band) or presence of bilateral edema indicates Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM). Children with medical complications or failed appetite test must be referred for inpatient stabilization.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Child 6–59 months with MUAC < 11.5 cm (Red band) OR Bilateral pitting edema of lower legs/feet (+, ++, +++).
danger_signs: Bilateral pitting edema extending to legs, hands, and face (+++ generalized edema)
Failed appetite test (unable to eat Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Food [RUTF])
High fever, hypothermia (<35.5 C), severe vomiting, or pneumonia symptoms
mandated_chw_actions: Perform gentle thumb pressure test on tops of both feet for 3 seconds to confirm pitting depression
If medical complications present or appetite test failed: Immediate emergency referral to hospital Inpatient Stabilization Unit
If alert, no complications, and appetite passed: Refer to nearest health facility Outpatient Therapeutic Program (OTP) for RUTF ration
Keep child warm; instruct caregiver to offer frequent small sips of sugar water during travel
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not administer high-protein adult family foods suddenly (triggers fatal refeeding syndrome)
Do not give standard adult vitamin iron supplements during initial acute phase (free radicals exacerbate sepsis)
Do not treat bilateral edema with diuretics (furosemide/lasix is contraindicated in kwashiorkor)

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-ICCM-09] Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM)
CRITERIA: Child 6-59m, MUAC < 11.5cm (RED) OR bilateral pitting edema.
ACTIONS: Check appetite. If sick or failed appetite: immediate hospital transfer. If alert: refer to OTP clinic for RUTF. Keep warm with sugar water.
PROHIBITED: Never give diuretics (Lasix) for nutritional edema. Do not give high-protein meals suddenly.

source_reference.manual: National Guideline for Integrated Management of Acute Malnutrition (IMAM)
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: A child aged 6 to 59 months with a MUAC between 11.5 cm and 12.4 cm (yellow color band) and no bilateral pitting edema is classified as having Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM). CHPs must refer the child to the Supplementary Feeding Program (SFP) for fortified blended flour/RUSF and conduct intensive infant and young child feeding (IYCF) counseling.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Child 6–59 months with MUAC >= 11.5 cm and <= 12.4 cm (Yellow band), NO edema, active and alert.
danger_signs: MUAC dropping towards 11.5 cm on serial tracking
Development of fever, cough, or diarrhea
New onset of foot swelling (transition to kwashiorkor)
mandated_chw_actions: Refer to dispensary for enrollment in Supplementary Feeding Program (SFP / RUSF / CSB++)
Counsel caregiver on active feeding: add locally available energy-dense foods (eggs, mashed legumes, groundnuts, milk, avocado)
Demonstrate enriched porridge preparation with oil and peanut paste
Schedule bi-weekly household MUAC monitoring until MUAC >= 12.5 cm on two consecutive visits
negative_boundaries: Do not share supplementary rations (RUSF) among family members (reserved exclusively for the malnourished child)
Do not replace ongoing breastfeeding with commercial infant formulas
Do not discharge from monitoring until green MUAC (>= 12.5 cm) is verified

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-ICCM-10] Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM)
CRITERIA: Child 6-59m, MUAC 11.5-12.4cm (YELLOW), no edema.
ACTIONS: Refer to dispensary for SFP/RUSF enrollment. Counsel on energy-dense complementary foods (eggs, milk, groundnut paste). Monitor MUAC every 2 weeks.
PROHIBITED: Do not share child's RUSF with household. Do not stop breastfeeding.

source_reference.manual: National Immunization Policy & Community Health Promoter Guide
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Every child in Kenya must receive all scheduled routine vaccines: Birth: BCG, OPV0; 6 weeks: Penta1, OPV1, PCV1, Rota1; 10 weeks: Penta2, OPV2, PCV2, Rota2; 14 weeks: Penta3, OPV3, PCV3, IPV; 6 months: Vitamin A; 9 months: Measles-Rubella 1 (MR1), Yellow Fever; 18 months: Measles-Rubella 2 (MR2); 10 years: HPV (girls). CHPs must inspect the Mother-Child Health Booklet at every visit.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: All infants and children residing in the community unit.
danger_signs: More than 4 weeks overdue for Penta3, PCV3, or IPV
Missed Measles-Rubella 1 at 9 months or MR2 at 18 months
Loss of Mother-Child Health booklet
mandated_chw_actions: Inspect the Mother-Child Health Booklet (MoH 216) and cross-reference dates against national schedule
Counsel parents on benefits of full immunization: protection against polio, pneumonia, rotavirus diarrhea, and measles
Refer and escort child to local dispensary on scheduled immunization clinic days
Record immunization status and next appointment in MoH 514 household register
negative_boundaries: Do not withhold vaccines due to mild minor illnesses (cough, cold, mild fever are NOT contraindications)
Do not charge any fees for routine KEPI vaccines (vaccines are 100% free at public facilities)
Do not advise skipping MR2 at 18 months even if child received MR1 at 9 months

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-EPI-01] National Immunization Schedule
CRITERIA: All children birth to 18m (+ HPV at 10y).
ACTIONS: Check booklet: Birth (BCG, OPV0); 6w, 10w, 14w (Penta, OPV, PCV, Rota, IPV); 9m (MR1, YF); 18m (MR2). Refer on clinic days. Record in MoH 514.
PROHIBITED: Never withhold vaccines for mild illness (colds). Vaccines are 100% free.

source_reference.manual: National Immunization Policy & Community Health Promoter Guide
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: A vaccine defaulter is any child who has missed a scheduled immunization by 2 weeks or more. CHPs must actively identify defaulters from facility defaulter registers and MoH 514, conduct physical household visits, and ensure the child completes missed doses. Never restart an interrupted vaccine schedule.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Child overdue for one or more scheduled vaccines by 14 days or longer.
danger_signs: Unvaccinated cluster of children in single neighborhood (outbreak risk)
Caregiver refusal due to misinformation or religious hesitancy
mandated_chw_actions: Perform physical home visit to understand underlying barrier (distance, clinic stockout, caregiver illness)
Explain catch-up policy: Child does NOT need to restart series from dose 1; simply administer the next due dose
Coordinate with local Community Health Assistant (CHA) to facilitate immediate catch-up at dispensary
Update household register (MoH 514) once dose is verified
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not restart the vaccine series from the beginning (continue from last validated dose)
Do not reprimand, fine, or humiliate caregivers for late presentation
Do not refuse catch-up vaccination to older children within approved catch-up age windows

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-EPI-02] Vaccine Defaulter Tracing
CRITERIA: Child overdue for scheduled vaccine by >=2 weeks.
ACTIONS: Conduct home visit. Address caregiver barriers. Escort to facility for catch-up. Reassure that schedule continues without restarting.
PROHIBITED: Never restart the series from dose 1. Do not scold or fine parents.

source_reference.manual: National Guidelines for Micronutrient Supplementation in Kenya
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: All children aged 6 to 59 months must receive high-dose Vitamin A supplementation every 6 months to reduce child mortality from measles and diarrhea. Age 6-11 months: 100,000 IU (blue capsule); Age 12-59 months: 200,000 IU (red capsule). Children aged 12 to 59 months must concurrently receive Deworming (Albendazole 400mg) every 6 months.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Children aged 6–59 months due for 6-monthly micronutrient supplementation.
danger_signs: Night blindness (inability to see in dim light), Bitot's spots, corneal clouding
Heavy intestinal helminth burden (potbelly, anemia, passing worms)
mandated_chw_actions: Verify last recorded Vitamin A and deworming date in Child Health booklet
Administer Vitamin A orally by cutting capsule nipple and expressing drops directly onto child's tongue:
- Age 6 to 11 months: Blue capsule (100,000 IU)
- Age 12 to 59 months: Red capsule (200,000 IU)
Administer Deworming tablet (Albendazole 400mg chewable or Mebendazole 500mg) for children >= 12 months
Crush deworming tablet for young toddlers to prevent choking
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not give red capsule (200,000 IU) to infants under 12 months
Do not administer deworming tablets (Albendazole) to infants under 12 months
Do not repeat Vitamin A if given within the last 1 month (hypervitaminosis risk)

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-EPI-03] Vitamin A & Deworming
CRITERIA: Children 6-59m, every 6 months.
ACTIONS: Vitamin A: 6-11m = Blue capsule (100k IU); 12-59m = Red capsule (200k IU). Deworming (Albendazole 400mg): children >=12m only (crush for toddlers). Record in booklet.
PROHIBITED: Never give red capsule or dewormer to infants <12 months. Do not repeat within 1 month.

source_reference.manual: National Immunization Policy & Community Health Promoter Guide
source_reference.section: Surveillance of Adverse Events Following Immunization
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: An AEFI is any untoward medical occurrence which follows immunization and does not necessarily have a causal relationship. CHPs must immediately report serious AEFIs (persistent screaming >3 hours, high fever >39 C, injection site abscess, convulsions, or collapse) to the health facility and Sub-County Coordinator within 24 hours.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Any child developing severe symptoms within 48 hours to 14 days following routine vaccination.
danger_signs: Persistent inconsolable screaming or crying lasting > 3 hours
High fever >= 39.0 C, convulsions, or limpness/hypotonic hyporesponsive episode
Large warm tender injection site swelling or fluctuant abscess
mandated_chw_actions: Provide immediate soothing and sponge with lukewarm water for fever
Urgent referral to health facility for clinical assessment and management
Notify Community Health Assistant (CHA) and Sub-County EPI focal person within 24 hours
Reassure family while maintaining trust in the broader immunization program
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not incise, lance, or squeeze injection site swelling or abscess
Do not apply herbal pastes, hot water compression, or animal dung to injection site
Do not counsel caregivers to permanently stop future routine vaccinations

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-EPI-04] AEFI Triage & Reporting
CRITERIA: Child with severe reaction post-immunization (fever >=39C, crying >3h, abscess, convulsions).
ACTIONS: Urgent referral to health facility. Sponge for fever. Report to sub-county focal person within 24 hours. Reassure caregiver.
PROHIBITED: Never incise or squeeze injection site swelling. Do not apply herbal poultices.

source_reference.manual: Kenya National Strategy for the Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Hypertension is a silent killer. All adults aged 18 years and above must have their blood pressure measured at least once every 6 months. High blood pressure is defined as Systolic BP >= 140 mmHg or Diastolic BP >= 90 mmHg. If elevated, allow the client to rest for 5 minutes and repeat measurement. Refer confirmed elevated clients to dispensary.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: All adults aged >= 18 years residing in the community unit.
danger_signs: Severe hypertensive urgency: Systolic BP >= 180 mmHg or Diastolic BP >= 110 mmHg
Severe occipital headache, blurred vision, chest pain, shortness of breath, acute limb weakness
mandated_chw_actions: Ensure client rests seated for 5 minutes in quiet room with legs uncrossed before measuring
Position arm supported at heart level with correct adult cuff size
If reading >= 140/90 mmHg: record, wait 5 minutes, and take second confirmatory reading
If confirmed >= 140/90 mmHg: Refer to nearest dispensary (Level 2/3) for clinical evaluation
Counsel on lifestyle modifications: reduce dietary salt to <5g/day (1 teaspoon), increase physical activity, avoid tobacco
negative_boundaries: Do not diagnose hypertension based on a single initial reading (always repeat after resting)
Do not prescribe or dispense anti-hypertensive tablets (Amlodipine, Enalapril) at home
Do not advise stopping medication if client reports feeling well

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-NCD-01] Adult Hypertension Screening
CRITERIA: Adults >=18y. Elevated BP: Systolic >=140 OR Diastolic >=90 mmHg.
ACTIONS: Rest 5 mins, repeat measurement. If confirmed >=140/90: refer to clinic. Counsel on low salt (<5g/day), exercise, weight, zero tobacco.
PROHIBITED: Never diagnose on single reading without rest. Do not dispense antihypertensives at home.

topic: Hypertension Adherence & Medication Refill Gap Tracking

source_reference.manual: Kenya National Strategy for the Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Hypertension requires continuous lifelong treatment. Patients who discontinue medication or experience refill gaps are at acute risk of rebound hypertension, stroke, and heart failure. CHPs must track clinic appointments and conduct home visits for any client who has missed their medication refill by 7 days or more.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Diagnosed hypertensive patients who have missed clinic refill dates by >=7 days or self-report stopping pills.
danger_signs: Rebound BP >= 160/100 mmHg with severe throbbing headache
Sudden facial droop, arm weakness, slurred speech (Signs of Acute Stroke — FAST criteria)
Chest pain radiating to left jaw or arm (Myocardial Infarction)
mandated_chw_actions: Measure current blood pressure and assess adherence over past month
Explore reason for default (drug stockout, side effects, transport cost, belief that disease is cured)
Reinforce that blood pressure control is lifelong and pills must be taken every single day even when asymptomatic
Provide referral slip (MoH 515) to replenish prescription at dispensary immediately
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not endorse switching to unverified herbal tonics, bitters, or garlic concoctions in place of prescription pills
Do not advise client to take double doses to make up for missed days
Do not tell client their hypertension is 'cured' because reading is currently normal on pills

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-NCD-02] Hypertension Adherence & Refill Gaps
CRITERIA: Known hypertensive patient with >=7 days refill gap or stopped medication.
ACTIONS: Measure BP. Check for stroke/chest pain red flags. Reiterate lifelong daily adherence. Escort to clinic for immediate prescription refill.
PROHIBITED: Never endorse stopping pills for herbal bitters. Do not take double doses. Normal BP on pills means control, not cure.

source_reference.manual: Kenya National Strategy for the Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: CHPs must screen adults for early symptoms of diabetes using the 4Ts: 1) Toilet (frequent urination, especially at night), 2) Thirsty (excessive unquenchable thirst), 3) Tired (unexplained fatigue), 4) Thinner (rapid unexplained weight loss). Clients with positive symptoms or random blood sugar >= 11.1 mmol/L must be referred for laboratory confirmation.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Adults reporting symptoms of polyuria, polydipsia, or unexplained weight loss, or high-risk individuals (overweight, family history).
danger_signs: Deep rapid Kussmaul breathing with sweet fruity breath odor (Diabetic Ketoacidosis [DKA])
Severe dehydration, drowsiness, confusion, or coma
Infected foot ulcers or gangrene
mandated_chw_actions: Screen for 4Ts: Toilet, Thirsty, Tired, Thinner
If glucometer available, perform fingerstick Random Blood Sugar (RBS): >= 11.1 mmol/L is highly suspicious
Refer client to health center for fasting plasma glucose (FPG >= 7.0 mmol/L) and HbA1c
Counsel on dietary changes: replace refined carbohydrates with whole grains; eliminate sugary sodas and sweets; daily physical activity
negative_boundaries: Do not diagnose diabetes on single random dipstick without formal clinic laboratory test
Do not initiate oral anti-diabetic medications (Metformin, Glibenclamide) at community level
Do not encourage restrictive starvation diets

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-NCD-03] Diabetes Screening (4Ts)
CRITERIA: Adults with 4Ts: Toilet (polyuria), Thirsty, Tired, Thinner, or RBS >= 11.1 mmol/L.
ACTIONS: Screen 4Ts. Check blood sugar if equipped. Refer to health center for fasting glucose/HbA1c. Counsel on whole grains, zero sugary sodas, exercise.
PROHIBITED: Never dispense Metformin/insulin at home. Do not promote unregulated herbal remedies.

source_reference.manual: Kenya National Strategy for the Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Hypoglycemia (blood sugar < 4.0 mmol/L) is an acute medical emergency in diabetic patients on insulin or sulfonylureas. Symptoms include profuse sweating, trembling, dizziness, intense hunger, and confusion. If conscious, give 15 grams of fast-acting sugar immediately. Diabetic clients must also have feet inspected for cracks, blisters, or ulcers at every visit.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Known diabetic patient presenting with acute cold sweat, shaking, confusion, or blood sugar < 4.0 mmol/L.
danger_signs: Loss of consciousness or convulsions from profound neuroglycopenia
Infected foot ulcer with redness, pus, or black tissue (gangrene)
mandated_chw_actions: Rule 15: If client is conscious and able to swallow, immediately administer 15-20g fast sugar (3 teaspoons table sugar in water, half glass fruit juice, or 3 sweets)
Wait 15 minutes and re-check blood sugar or clinical state; follow with small carbohydrate snack (bread, porridge)
Inspect feet: Check between toes, heels, and soles for cuts, blisters, corns, or loss of protective sensation
Urgent referral to facility if ulcer identified or recurrent hypoglycemia occurs
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not give insulin during a suspected hypoglycemia episode (will cause fatal coma)
Do not force liquids into an unconscious client's mouth (high aspiration pneumonia risk)
Do not cut corns or apply hot water bottles to numb diabetic feet

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-NCD-04] Hypoglycemia & Diabetic Foot Care
CRITERIA: Diabetic client with shakiness, cold sweat, confusion, or RBS < 4.0 mmol/L.
ACTIONS: Rule 15: If conscious, give 3 tsp sugar in water or fruit juice immediately. Recheck in 15 mins. Inspect feet for ulcers. Refer recurrent episodes.
PROHIBITED: NEVER give insulin during low sugar. Do not pour fluids in unconscious mouth. No hot water bottles on feet.

source_reference.manual: Kenya Mental Health Policy & Community Integration Framework
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Mental health is an integral component of primary health care. CHPs must identify common mental disorders including depression, severe anxiety, and psychosis using simple behavioral observation. Clients presenting with persistent low mood (>2 weeks), withdrawal, hallucinations, or expressions of self-harm must be connected to mental health services.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Adolescents or adults exhibiting persistent changes in behavior, mood, social withdrawal, or distress.
danger_signs: Expressed plans or intent of suicide or self-harm
Acute agitation, confusion, or visual/auditory hallucinations
Complete neglect of basic hygiene, infant care, or nourishment
mandated_chw_actions: Provide a calm, safe, non-judgmental space and listen with empathy
If suicidal intent is detected: never leave the individual alone; remove dangerous items (pesticides, ropes, sharp tools); engage a trusted family member immediately
Facilitate referral to health facility mental health focal point or counselor
Screen postpartum mothers for maternal blues vs postpartum psychosis
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not dismiss symptoms as bewitchment, curses, or moral/spiritual weakness
Do not lock or chain individuals with mental health conditions
Do not administer sedative medications or traditional intoxicating concoctions

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-NCD-05] Community Mental Health & Depression
CRITERIA: Persistent low mood (>2w), withdrawal, distress, or psychosis.
ACTIONS: Provide calm, non-judgmental listening. If self-harm risk: never leave alone, remove pesticides/ropes, involve family. Refer to mental health clinic.
PROHIBITED: Never dismiss as bewitchment. Do not lock or chain patients. Do not give unauthorized sedatives.

source_reference.manual: National Family Planning Guidelines for Service Providers
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Oral contraceptive pills are safe and effective when taken consistently every day. Combined Oral Contraceptives (COCs) contain estrogen and progestin and are contraindicated in breastfeeding women under 6 months postpartum. Progestin-Only Pills (POPs) are the method of choice for lactating mothers starting at 6 weeks postpartum.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Women of reproductive age (15–49 years) requesting short-acting hormonal contraception for pregnancy spacing.
danger_signs: Elevated blood pressure >= 140/90 mmHg (Contraindication for COCs)
Severe migraine headache with aura (visual disturbance)
Known liver disease or active thromboembolism (blood clots)
mandated_chw_actions: Screen using medical eligibility checklist: If breastfeeding <6 months, dispense POP (Microval) instead of COC
If non-breastfeeding and normotensive: Dispense COC (Microlut/Microgynon) pack
Instruct client to take exactly 1 pill daily at the same time each day (set phone alarm or bedtime cue)
Explain missed pill protocol: If 1 pill missed, take as soon as remembered and next at regular time
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not dispense COCs to breastfeeding mothers within 6 weeks of delivery (inhibits lactation)
Do not dispense COCs to women with BP >= 140/90 or age > 35 who smoke
Do not tell client pills cause permanent infertility or birth defects

prompt_injection_chunk:
