### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-FP-01] Oral Contraceptive Pills (COC & POP)
CRITERIA: Women 15-49y seeking child spacing.
ACTIONS: Screen BP. Breastfeeding <6m: give POPs. Non-breastfeeding & normotensive: give COCs. Take 1 pill daily at exact same time.
PROHIBITED: Never give COCs if BP >=140/90 or breastfeeding <6 weeks. Pills do not cause infertility.

source_reference.manual: National Family Planning Guidelines for Service Providers
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Sayana Press (DMPA-SC 104mg/0.65ml) is a single-use prefilled injection system administered subcutaneously every 13 weeks. CHPs trained and certified in community administration may administer or support self-injection. The injection site must never be massaged as this accelerates drug absorption and shortens contraceptive coverage.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Women 15–49 years seeking 3-month discrete injectable child spacing, reasonably certain not pregnant.
danger_signs: Unexplained abnormal vaginal bleeding before injection
Active jaundice, severe hypertension (>160/100), or current breast cancer
mandated_chw_actions: Verify non-pregnancy (rule of pregnancy checklist)
Mix solution by shaking unit vigorously for 30 seconds; activate device by pressing needle guard into port
Pinch skin of abdomen (>=5cm from navel) or anterior thigh; insert needle fully at 45 degree angle; squeeze reservoir slowly over 5 seconds
Dispose of used Uniject in certified safety box immediately
Record appointment date for next injection in exactly 13 weeks (3 months)
negative_boundaries: ABSOLUTE PROHIBITION: Never rub or massage the injection site after administration (shortens efficacy)
Do not administer if the Uniject liquid is clumpy or does not form uniform white suspension after shaking
Do not recap needle or throw used device into open domestic rubbish pit

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-FP-02] Sayana Press (DMPA-SC)
CRITERIA: Women 15-49y requesting 3-month injectable contraception.
ACTIONS: Shake 30s. Inject subcutaneously into abdomen or thigh over 5s. Discard in safety box. Schedule reinjection in exactly 13 weeks.
PROHIBITED: ABSOLUTE PROHIBITION: NEVER massage the injection site. Do not discard in open trash.

source_reference.manual: National Family Planning Guidelines for Service Providers
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Long-Acting Reversible Contraceptives (LARCs) including sub-dermal implants (Jadelle 5-year, Implanon 3-year) and Copper Intrauterine Devices (IUD 10-12 years) provide the highest contraceptive efficacy with minimal daily user adherence. CHPs must provide comprehensive counseling, dispel myths, and refer clients to health facilities for sterile clinical insertion.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Women seeking highly effective multi-year pregnancy prevention without daily or quarterly tasks.
danger_signs: Suspected current pelvic infection (foul discharge, severe lower abdominal tenderness)
Known uterine anomalies or active pelvic inflammatory disease
mandated_chw_actions: Provide unbiased balanced counseling comparing Implants (3-5 years) vs Copper IUD (10-12 years)
Address common cultural myths: reassure that IUDs do not travel to the heart or brain, and implants do not cause cancer
Explain side effects: spotting or light bleeding in initial months is common and benign
Refer and accompany client to dispensary or health center for clinical insertion by a qualified nurse/midwife
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not attempt to insert or remove subdermal implants or IUDs at home
Do not deny LARC counseling to nulliparous or young unmarried women
Do not promise complete absence of menstrual changes

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-FP-03] LARC Counseling (Implants & IUD)
CRITERIA: Women seeking multi-year protection (Implants 3-5y, IUD 10-12y).
ACTIONS: Counsel on benefits and return to fertility. Dispel myths (IUD does not travel; implants do not cause cancer). Refer to health facility for insertion.
PROHIBITED: Never attempt home insertion/removal. Do not deny counseling to nulliparous youth.

source_reference.manual: National Family Planning Guidelines for Service Providers
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Emergency Contraceptive Pills (Levonorgestrel 1.5mg single dose) prevent pregnancy following unprotected sexual intercourse, condom breakage, or sexual assault if taken within 120 hours (5 days). ECP is most effective when taken within the first 24 hours. CHPs must also distribute condoms to provide dual protection against STIs and HIV.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Unprotected intercourse or barrier failure occurring within the preceding 120 hours.
danger_signs: Sexual assault / gender-based violence (requires Post-Exposure Prophylaxis [PEP] within 72 hours and emergency STI management)
Severe unilateral lower pelvic pain 3-5 weeks post-ECP (suspected ectopic pregnancy)
mandated_chw_actions: Administer Levonorgestrel 1.5mg (Postinor-2 / single tablet) as soon as possible, within 120 hours
If sexual assault: Escort immediately to facility for GBV management (PEP for HIV within 72h, emergency contraception, Hepatitis B, forensic exam)
Distribute male and female condoms and demonstrate correct usage for dual protection
Transition client to a continuous regular family planning method for ongoing protection
negative_boundaries: Do not promote or utilize ECP as a regular monthly contraceptive method
Do not state or imply ECP causes abortion (it prevents ovulation; it does NOT terminate an established pregnancy)
Do not delay administration to wait for a specific time of day

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-FP-04] Emergency Contraception (ECP) & Condoms
CRITERIA: Unprotected sex within 120 hours (5 days).
ACTIONS: Give Levonorgestrel 1.5mg ASAP (best <24h). Distribute condoms for dual protection. If sexual assault: immediate facility transfer for HIV PEP within 72h.
PROHIBITED: ECP is not an abortion pill. Do not use as regular monthly contraception.

source_reference.manual: Community Event-Based Surveillance (CEBS) Field Guide
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Any child under 15 years who develops sudden floppy weakness in one or more limbs without trauma is a suspected case of Polio (AFP). Every AFP case must be notified immediately to the Sub-County Disease Surveillance Coordinator within 24 hours. Two stool specimens must be collected 24 to 48 hours apart within 14 days of paralysis onset.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Sudden onset of floppy (flaccid) weakness of arms or legs in a child < 15 years, not caused by recent injury or trauma.
danger_signs: Rapidly ascending paralysis involving respiratory muscles or swallowing difficulty
Multiple children in same village developing limb weakness
mandated_chw_actions: Immediate verbal phone and eCHIS alert to the Community Health Assistant (CHA) and Sub-County Disease Surveillance Coordinator (SCDSC) within 24 hours
Assist surveillance team in tracking the child and collecting 2 adequate stool specimens 24-48 hours apart
Check immunization card for Polio vaccines (OPV/IPV) and investigate recent travel
Reassure family and maintain close community surveillance
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not give intramuscular injections into the paralyzed limb (exacerbates nerve damage)
Do not massage paralyzed limbs with hot stones or traditional oils
Do not delay notification past 24 hours

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-CEBS-01] Acute Flaccid Paralysis (AFP / Polio)
CRITERIA: Child <15y with sudden floppy weakness in limbs without trauma.
ACTIONS: Immediate alert to Sub-County Surveillance Coordinator within 24 hours. Assist collecting 2 stool samples 24-48h apart. Check OPV/IPV history.
PROHIBITED: ABSOLUTE PROHIBITION: Never give intramuscular injections into paralyzed limb. No hot stones.

topic: Cholera & Acute Watery Diarrhea Cluster Early Warning

source_reference.manual: Community Event-Based Surveillance (CEBS) Field Guide
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Any patient aged 2 years or older who presents with sudden profuse watery diarrhea ('rice water' stools) and rapid severe dehydration, OR any cluster of 2 or more individuals with severe acute watery diarrhea in the same village within 5 days, constitutes a suspected Cholera outbreak. Immediate reporting to the sub-county within 12 hours is mandatory.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Person >=2 years with sudden onset watery diarrhea resembling rice-water OR clustering of 2+ cases in single village.
danger_signs: Rapid hypovolemic shock (unconscious, feeble pulse, cold skin, zero urine output within hours)
Concurrent severe vomiting with muscle cramps from severe electrolyte depletion
mandated_chw_actions: Immediately alert Community Health Assistant and Sub-County Surveillance team within 12 hours
Start continuous Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) administration immediately while organizing emergency transport
Distribute chlorine tablets (WaterGuard) to the index household and surrounding 20 homes
Instruct family to dedicate a single latrine and disinfect surfaces with chlorine solution
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not wash contaminated clothes or bedding in local rivers, open streams, or community ponds
Do not organize communal gatherings, funerals, or shared feasts without strict public health supervision
Do not wait for laboratory stool culture before initiating rehydration and community notification

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-CEBS-02] Cholera / Acute Watery Diarrhea Outbreak
CRITERIA: Person >=2y with rice-water diarrhea OR 2+ cases in same village.
ACTIONS: Alert sub-county within 12 hours. Continuous ORS. Isolate latrine. Disinfect with chlorine. Distribute WaterGuard to surrounding 20 homes.
PROHIBITED: Never wash soiled items in rivers/streams. Do not wait for lab culture before starting ORS and alerts.

source_reference.manual: Community Event-Based Surveillance (CEBS) Field Guide
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: A suspected measles case is any person presenting with fever and a generalized maculopapular rash, plus at least one of the 3Cs: Cough, Coryza (runny nose), or Conjunctivitis (red inflamed eyes). A cluster of 3 or more suspected cases within a community unit indicates an active outbreak requiring immediate notification.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Any individual with fever and generalized non-vesicular rash plus cough, coryza, or red eyes.
danger_signs: Corneal ulceration / opacity leading to blindness
Deep chest indrawing or stridor (severe post-measles pneumonia)
Severe mouth ulcers, inability to eat, and acute nutritional wasting
mandated_chw_actions: Notify Community Health Assistant and Sub-County focal person immediately
Administer age-appropriate Vitamin A dose immediately (reduces blindness and mortality by 50%)
Isolate child in ventilated room to prevent airborne transmission to vulnerable infants
Screen all neighborhood children under 5 years for missing MR1 and MR2 vaccines
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not administer traditional herbal eyewashes or concoctions into inflamed eyes
Do not confine child in dark, unventilated smoky huts (damages respiratory mucosa)
Do not administer aspirin to febrile children (risk of fatal Reye's syndrome)

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-CEBS-03] Suspected Measles Outbreak
CRITERIA: Fever + generalized rash + at least one of: Cough, Coryza, Red eyes.
ACTIONS: Immediate alert to sub-county. Administer Vitamin A dose immediately. Isolate child in airy room. Screen neighborhood for missed MR1/MR2.
PROHIBITED: No traditional herbal eyewashes. Never give aspirin to febrile children.

source_reference.manual: Maternal and Perinatal Death Surveillance and Response (MPDSR) Guidelines
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Every death of a woman of reproductive age (15-49 years) during pregnancy, childbirth, or within 42 days of delivery, and every stillbirth or neonatal death occurring in the community must be notified within 24 hours. The goal is to identify systemic breakdowns and prevent future preventable deaths.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Any death of a woman while pregnant or within 42 days of termination, or death of a newborn within first 28 days of life occurring in the community.
danger_signs: Surviving newborn without immediate caregiver or feeding plan
Severe maternal hemorrhage, obstructed labor, or sepsis prior to death
mandated_chw_actions: Notify Community Health Assistant and Sub-County Reproductive Health Coordinator within 24 hours
Provide compassionate grief support to the bereaved family without judgment
Ensure surviving infant is protected, kept warm, and provided with safe newborn feeding plan
Assist public health team in scheduling a sensitive Maternal and Perinatal Death Verbal Autopsy
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not assign personal blame, guilt, or shame to the mother or family
Do not record misleading causes of death without medical audit team review
Do not neglect the welfare and urgent nutritional needs of a surviving infant

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-ECHIS-CEBS-04] Maternal & Perinatal Death Audit
CRITERIA: Death of woman during pregnancy/within 42 days, or neonate within 28 days.
ACTIONS: Notify sub-county within 24 hours for MPDSR verbal autopsy. Provide compassionate family support. Secure immediate safe care for surviving baby.
PROHIBITED: Never assign blame or shame to family. Do not neglect surviving newborn.
